Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0001] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: When a repo has a dedicated money helper (e.g. ledgerly.money.round_money), route every monetary result through it rather than relying on Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
[ace-0003] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: Before implementing, read the module's existing helpers and sibling functions (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to mirror their conventions for conversion (to_money), rounding, and zero handling.
[ace-0004] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When validating integer inputs, explicitly reject bool (isinstance(x, bool)) since bool is a subclass of int; also reject non-int types like float before comparing.
[ace-0005] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Mirror the error codes and message formats used by sibling functions (e.g. invalid_state with f"invoice {id} is {status}") so new validation paths stay consistent with the codebase's BillingError conventions.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0002] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: For weighted-average or division-based money computations, round only the final result with the project's money helper; do not round intermediate sums, and return the project's ZERO constant for empty/zero-denominator cases.
[ace-0006] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Don't assume round_money/to_money accepts arbitrary types silently; verify behavior with edge inputs (floats, strings) and rely on the helper to raise the project's error (e.g. float_amount) rather than duplicating type checks.

item.content: For 'first occurrence strictly after X' recurrence problems, compute n = (after - start) // length + 1 and return start + n*length; handle the after < start case separately (return start + length) since floor division on negative timedeltas can misbehave.

When a sibling function (e.g. current_period) already normalizes datetimes via ensure_utc and builds timedelta(days=period_days), reuse the exact same normalization and arithmetic in the new function so timezone handling and boundary semantics stay consistent.

In ledgerly, Subscription.period_days is typed int but may arrive as bool or non-positive; validate with isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool) plus x > 0, raising BillingError('invalid_period', repr(x)).
